body:
HARD PRODUCT REVIEW — I CRITIQUED THE ARTIFACT AS ASKED, AND I AM ANSWERING ONLY THE TWO QUESTIONS
THAT ARE MINE. Q1 and Q2 are chief acceptance decisions and I will not answer for the chief.

THE ARTIFACT, MEASURED, not impressions:

  /private/tmp/storyatlas-preview-qa.p32XrG/edition/preview.html   170,455 bytes
    <g> elements            648
    <span> elements          46
    <svg>                     2
    data-name attributes    694
    aria-* / role= / tabindex  ZERO

Q3 — VISUALIZATION. THE PROPOSED FLOOR IS NOT MET, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN
COSMETIC, BUT THE GAP IS SMALLER THAN "REJECT AND REBUILD".

The floor says "click or keyboard-select a text span". THERE IS NOTHING TO SELECT. Zero tabindex and
zero role/aria across 170KB means no element is focusable and none has an accessible name. A keyboard
user cannot reach any of the 694 named things, and a screen reader is told nothing about any of them.
That is not a styling gap; the interaction the floor requires has no attachment point.

BUT THE ADDRESSABILITY ALREADY EXISTS AND SHOULD NOT BE THROWN AWAY. 694 `data-name` attributes means
the generator already knows, per element, what each mark IS. The artifact is ONE LAYER SHORT: it can
NAME 694 elements and cannot let a reader REACH or INTERROGATE one. That is a layer to add, not a
preview to discard, and I would not accept a decision to rebuild from zero on this evidence.

On "dominated by dense gray bands": 648 groups inside 2 SVGs with a single legend is consistent with
that complaint. The per-element identity is present in the DOM and absent from the rendering.

NOW THE PART ONLY I CAN GIVE YOU, AND IT CHANGES WHAT THE FLOOR CAN HONESTLY PROMISE.

The floor asks a selected span to show "missing/imputed/suppressed status". In align today:

  MEASURED    derivable    CostBreakdown.terms
  ABSENT      derivable    CostBreakdown.missingTerms
  IMPUTED     derivable    CostBreakdown.imputedTerms, with the provider's MissingReason (0ca09c5)
  INELIGIBLE  NOT DERIVABLE, and NOT reconstructible as a complement

Eligibility is computed inside `cost()` and thrown away. On a chartless cell, Chart is BOTH recorded
missing AND excluded from eligible, so "absent" and "this cell never had this dimension" are the same
bytes in the published record. A viewer that renders a four-way status today would have to guess
between them and would be wrong roughly half the time, silently. THAT IS THE EXACT FAILURE vision.md
rejects — a confident answer in place of an examinable one.

SO THE HONEST FLOOR IS A THREE-WAY STATUS PLUS A NAMED FOURTH THAT THE RECORD CANNOT YET SUPPORT.
I would rather ship a viewer that says "this system cannot currently tell you whether this dimension
was inapplicable" than one that quietly picks a bucket.

AND ONE NUMBER ON THAT PANEL WOULD BE FALSE TODAY. If a selected cell shows support, it reads
`supportWeight`. Every external row is built at hsmm.scala:597 with defaults, carrying terms EMPTY
and supportWeight 1.0. In the WOG golden: 18 breakdowns, 10 with terms empty and support 1.0, ZERO
with non-empty terms and support 1.0. In that corpus the maximum support value has never once meant
full support. A reader clicking an external cell would be told "fully supported" about a cell that
measured nothing. bd-01M19956, unassigned.

Q4 — SEQUENCING, align side only. If the inspectable visualization court is the goal, then the
support repair and the eligibility carrier are PRECONDITIONS, not follow-ups. Build the viewer first
and you will render a false number and an underivable status, then have to un-teach both. The
cheapest honest order is: fix what the record can say, then show it.

WHAT I AM NOT SAYING: that the visualization should wait for all of align. Three of the four statuses
are derivable now, spans are exact on both sides — RecallUnit.span and NodeSummary.support are real
SpanSets — and CellCoordinates already joins them with checksum proof. A viewer built on THOSE, with
the fourth status named as unavailable and support omitted until repaired, is buildable today and
would be honest.
